headlines: NEW SENIOR AFFORDABLE HOUSING PROPOSED IN MIAMI-DADE COUNTY
71 AFFORDABLE SENIOR APARTMENTS PLANNED FOR MIAMI-DADE
MIAMI LAKES DEVELOPER EYES NEW SEVEN-STORY SENIOR HOUSING VENTURE
draft.article: Miami Lakes-based Centennial Management Corp., through affiliate LVS Naranja LLC, has filed a pre-application for Redland Crossing Senior Living in Miami-Dade County. The proposed 70,000-square-foot development will rise seven stories on a 0.79-acre site located west of the Redland Crossings apartment complex. Gallo Herbert Architecture designed the building, which will feature 71 affordable apartments offering one-bedroom and two-bedroom layouts. Planned amenities include a clubroom, a fitness center, and 41 parking spaces. Every unit will serve residents earning at or below 140 percent of the area median income, which stands at $87,200 as of 2025. The venture is currently gathering community feedback prior to formal application filing.

headlines: JOSÉ ANDRÉS OPENS BAZAAR MEAT AT ANDAZ MIAMI BEACH
BAZAAR MEAT BRINGS LIVE FIRE TO COLLINS AVENUE
CHEF JOSÉ ANDRÉS RETURNS TO MID-BEACH WITH NEW STEAKHOUSE
draft.article:
Chef José Andrés has officially returned to our shores, opening Bazaar Meat on Collins Avenue on the ground floor of the Andaz Miami Beach in Mid-Beach.

The theatrical live-fire steakhouse marks an exciting comeback after his original Beach concept closed in 2023 following an 11-year run at the SLS South Beach. Culinary director Manuel Manny Echeverri leads the kitchen day to day.

Inside the maximalist dining room designed by Spain's Lázaro Rosa-Violán Studio, the kitchen showcases dry-aged meats grilled over an open flame. The menu features signature bites, including a Miami-exclusive Cubano airbread and a tableside martini cart, joining Andrés' other resort concepts, Aguasal and Bar Centro.

items.desc: The Lucy Project focuses on high-need schools. The share of 3rd graders who are "proficient or above" at the five schools with the new hubs is less than 55% at each school, according to state data from last school year.

headlines: NONPROFIT EXPANDS TO NINE MIAMI SCHOOLS AFTER READING SURGE
MIAMI STUDENTS ARE BEATING THE ODDS IN READING
HOW MIAMI GARDENS KINDERGARTENERS HIT AN 88 PERCENT LITERACY RATE
draft.article:
A major literacy initiative is rapidly growing across Miami-Dade County classrooms. The Lucy Project, led by founder Sandra Bermudez, is expanding into five additional elementary campuses this year after driving dramatic academic gains at Norwood Elementary in Miami Gardens. At Norwood, kindergarten reading proficiency surged from 52 percent to 88 percent in two years.

Backed by a $500,000 donation from the Partnership for Miami, the program now reaches nine campuses, including Riverside, Broadmoor, Melrose, James H. Bright, and Laura C. Sanders elementary schools, plus Liberty Academy for pre-K.

Costing approximately $1,500 per kindergartner, the organization uses evidence-based phonics instruction to assist local schools where third-grade proficiency rates sit under 55 percent.

The Miami Dolphins travel to the Meadowlands this Sunday to battle the New York Jets in their first AFC East contest of 2026. This marks the 122nd meeting in the long rivalry, with Miami holding a 63-57-1 series advantage. It is the first time since 2013 that Miami had to wait until Week 7 for its opening divisional matchup.

Coming off an early bye week, Miami now begins a demanding stretch of 12 straight games to close the campaign. Head Coach Jeff Hafley noted the squad returned locked in with exceptional energy. headlines: CANALS BEGAN DRAINING THE FLORIDA EVERGLADES IN 1906
1906 MARKS THE START OF EVERGLADES CANAL DRAINING
HOW WATER REMOVAL FROM THE EVERGLADES BEGAN IN 1906
draft.article: In 1906, major excavation work began as canals were initiated to remove water from the Florida Everglades. This period marked the early groundwork that would reshape the landscape just west of the growing Miami area. The start of these canals in 1906 officially launched the process of draining the vast Everglades wetlands. As digging began that year, the removal of water altered the natural flow throughout the historic Everglades ecosystem.
